messages:
alex (infra): :rotating_light: Getting multiple escalations: p95/p99 for /v1/generate and /v1/embeddings spiking since ~03:10 UTC. Tickets from 3 different customers reporting slow responses and timeouts. Root infra metrics show tail latency jump across several GPU nodes.

maya (sre): noted. Which fleet/region? Any recent infra changes?

alex (infra): eu-west-1 GPU pool A. We rolled a small infra kernel + driver patch in the maintenance window at 02:50 UTC (driver v530.41 -> v531.12, host kernel backports). Can someone bisect?

ben (support): customer_jane reports 10–20x p99 increase for embeddings; sample request ids: req_3f9a, req_b8e3. Attached a curl repro. They said it started after midday.

maya (sre): I'm pulling per-node p99s now. Running iostat/dstat and checking nvme latencies. Will also correlate with rollout map.

oncall-bot: Incident created: INC-2026-03-15-1987654321. Paging oncall.

julian (eng-runtime): If this is storage IO tail, we might see long kv cache evictions during checkpoint/dump. Any heavy checkpoints around that time?

tara (eng-ml): We did a scheduled model shard checkpoint to persistent store at 02:57 UTC for a few training jobs in eu-west-1 (non-prod). That could align.

maya (sre): Quick findings: on nodes gpu-az1-12 and gpu-az1-14 nvme_ns read/write latency spikes concurrent with the p99 increase. iostat output (trimmed):
```
Device            r/s     w/s   rkB/s   wkB/s await  svctm  %util
nvme0n1         1000   4800  102400  512000  45.2   2.10  98.7
```
Also dmesg shows occasional blk_update_timeouts.

julian (eng-runtime): nvidia-smi and process lists? Maybe driver/CUDA introduced a path that serializes IO for certain NVMe controller combos.

maya (sre): nvidia-smi looks normal for GPU usage, but we see heavy CPU steal as storage tasks block. Running strace on runtime worker shows long epoll_wait during write calls to leveldb/rocksdb.

alex (infra): Rollout map confirms driver v531.12 deployed to that pool at 02:50 in a canary then live. Any nodes still on v530?

maya (sre): Found a node still on v530. Rewinding one node to v530 as a quick test.

julian (eng-runtime): Good. If p99 drops on that node, we have a strong signal.

maya (sre): Reverted node gpu-az1-14 to v530.41 at 03:22 UTC. Measuring... p99 for that node dropped from 1.8s to 210ms for the same traffic pattern. Other nodes still at 1.6–2.1s.

ben (support): customer_jane confirmed improved latency for the requests routed to gpu-az1-14 after the revert. They still see slow responses hitting other nodes.

tara (eng-ml): So driver looks implicated. But why storage IO? Any kernel messages?

maya (sre): Checking kernel logs: after v531 install there's a backported change in block layer queue behavior (changed default queue_depth to 1024 and different submission path). NVMe GC on some controllers seems to be getting triggered more aggressively under our workload, causing long flushes. dmesg snippet: 
```
[Mar15 03:05] nvme 0000:3b:00.0: nvme_irq: controller error, code 0x9
[Mar15 03:06] blk_update_request: I/O error, dev nvme0n1, sector 123456789
```

julian (eng-runtime): Interesting — newer driver maybe changes submission or flush behavior that interacts poorly with this NVMe firmware. We also have async checkpointer doing concurrent filefsyncs which amplify queue pressure.

alex (infra): Action plan short term: 1) pause rollout (we stopped remaining hosts at 02:58) 2) roll back fleet to v530 where possible 3) rate-limit checkpoint concurrency 4) steer traffic off affected nodes via routing.

maya (sre): Implemented routing shift: mark nodes in pool A as unhealthy for /generate and /embeddings at 03:30 UTC. That dropped global p99 from ~1.7s to ~350ms.

julian (eng-runtime): Implemented a hotfix in runtime: reduce concurrent checkpoint writer threads from 8 -> 2 and enable small batching for flushes. Deployed config at 03:35 UTC. This reduces write bursts to NVMe.

ben (support): Customers on impacted tickets reporting improved results after 03:36 UTC. Sending status updates. :thumbsup:

maya (sre): Next diagnostics: we need to bisect driver vs kernel vs NVMe firmware. Can we repro in lab?

alex (infra): Spun up a repro cluster with same NVMe model and applied v531 and v530 alternately. Repro steps documented in the runbook. Observed same tail latencies under heavy concurrent fsync workload only on v531.

julian (eng-runtime): In lab I instrumented block-layer latency and saw a pattern: with v531 the median queue depth jumps and long tail latencies appear when concurrent small fsyncs occur. Code snippet used to generate load: 
```
for i in 1..N:
  write 16MB file
  fsync(fd)
```
Using N=200 in parallel reproduces the tail.

tara (eng-ml): We confirmed our checkpointer uses parallel syncs; we can change it to stream shards one-by-one until we have a permanent fix. 

maya (sre): Immediate mitigations carried out: 
- Reverted ~70% of the fleet to v530.41 (03:40 UTC).
- Paused remaining rollout.
- Runtime config change to throttle checkpoint concurrency (03:35 UTC).
- Routing: removed affected hosts from LB for critical APIs (03:30 UTC).
- Temporary increase of read-only cache TTLs and enabled local KV prefix caching to reduce writes (03:42 UTC).

alex (infra): Long-term items: 
- Work with driver vendor and NVMe vendor to identify firmware interaction (open ticket with NVMe vendor).
- Add a pre-rollout IO microbenchmark (fsync storm) to rollout gating.
- Add NVMe SMART / latency alerting on %util and queue depth to catch this earlier.
- Re-evaluate kernel backport that changes queue submission; consider pinning kernel for next release.

julian (eng-runtime): Also adding a runtime safeguard: if local disk write latency > 200ms for 30s, automatically reduce checkpoint concurrency and route traffic away. Will PR today.

ben (support): Notifying affected customers of mitigation and follow-up plan. Sending a timeline and ETA for final resolution.

oncall-bot: Update: incident severity reduced to S2 at 04:05 UTC.

maya (sre): Closing actions for now: I will continue monitoring nvme latency and driver rollout. If vendor provides a firmware/driver patch, we'll test in lab before any more rollout.

alex (infra): Thanks all. Postmortem owners: maya (lead), julian (runtime fix), alex (rollout gating), tara (checkpoint changes), ben (customer comms).

customer_jane: Thanks team — appreciate fast response and temporary fixes.

maya (sre): I'll draft the incident report and include the repro steps, commands, and timelines. Pushed a short runbook update to the repo.

alex (infra): Quick-save of useful commands used during debug: 
```
# nvme latency
sudo iostat -x 1
sudo nvme list
sudo nvme smart-log /dev/nvme0n1
# block layer
dmesg | grep nvme
journalctl -k -u kubelet
# reproduce load
./fsync_storm --parallel 200 --filesize 16M
```

maya (sre): last check: p99 stabilized at ~320ms for critical APIs after rollback+mitigations (04:12 UTC). I'll keep monitoring and post updates in the incident doc. :white_check_mark:
